claims.text: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the driver must carry limb (c) on its own words: he must have 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' the 300 seconds the fee schedule sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The driver's own 10-second telemetry records exactly two in-geofence holds, 170 seconds from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds from 18:49:35, each reported as a separate run. The longest continuous hold anywhere in this pickup is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short of the minimum, and the rider's description of a car that 'kept moving around' and never 'stayed 5 minutes in one place' is precisely what the trace records.

The only route by which the driver reaches 300 seconds is the summing of the two holds permitted by POL-NS-06(i), and that permission is conditional: the trace must show the driver leaving and re-entering the arrival radius 'without at any point travelling more than 300 m from the pin'. Over this pickup (18:39:05 to 18:52:40) the trace summary reports a maximum distance from the pin of 1,191.8 m - some four times the leash - and a total track of 3.0 km. The smaller 179.0 m figure reported for the inter-interval excursion is not the driver's maximum range on the trace. If the leash is applied to the trace as its words 'at any point' require, the condition for accumulation is not made out, the intervals cannot be summed, and the effective dwell remains the single 185-second hold.

Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the POL-NS-02 geofence at or before the timestamp of the arrival event. The event is logged at 18:44:30, while the earliest qualifying in-radius fix on the driver's own trace opens the first qualifying run at 18:44:45 - fifteen seconds later, and more than one 10-second sampling interval behind the marker. The record therefore carries no admissible in-radius fix at or before the marker to support the condition that marker certifies, and the waiting clock under POL-NS-01(c) runs from the first qualifying fix at 18:44:45, not from the marker.

trip_record.wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is not dwell: it is elapsed time from the 18:44:30 marker to the 18:52:45 cancellation, 495 seconds in all. Across that period the trace accounts for only 355 seconds inside the arrival radius; the balancing 140 seconds is time outside the geofence, including the 120-second loop between 18:47:35 and 18:49:35 during which the driver reached 179 m from the pin and speeds of up to 49.6 km/h. A 'wait' figure built on the marker cannot supply the continuous 300-second hold POL-NS-01(c) requires.

The rider does not press POL-NS-04, and says so plainly rather than stretching it: her 18:46:20 message was followed by the driver's 18:47:50 reply, ninety seconds later, so limb (b)'s 120-second-silence requirement is not met and the clause cannot run in her favour. This case is decided on the dwell arithmetic under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06, not on the contact clause.

The contested sum is the cancellation-fee line alone. fare_breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Where the effective dwell falls short of the POL-NS-01 minimum for the zone class, POL-NS-06 refunds that line to the rider in full and states that no driver compensation is payable. The rider seeks SGD 4.00 returned and no compensation paid out of it; the fee is the only amount the ledger moved.

claims.text: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-08-07T18:44:30, and the GPS trace then places the driver inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius of 120 m from 18:44:45, generating 40 qualifying in-radius fixes across two separate holds (18:44:45-18:47:35 and 18:49:35-18:52:40). That is far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires before arrival is deemed established, so POL-NS-01 limb (a) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are both satisfied on the trace's own numbers.

There is no false arrival marker to attack. Nothing in the record places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h or above at the 18:44:30 marker: the derived excursion block measures the driver's furthest point between the two holds at 178.95 m, and it records the POL-NS-06(i) limb as available rather than flagging any false-arrival condition. Even on the rider's best case that the marker preceded the first in-radius fix by a single 10 second sampling interval, POL-NS-05(iii) applies: the waiting clock is recomputed to the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45, and because the corrected dwell still exceeds the 300 second minimum the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 355 accumulated seconds - two holds of 170 s and 185 s - against the LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 s. The derived shortfall is minus 55 seconds, meaning there is no shortfall at all, so POL-NS-06 returns no refund. The rider's assertion that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' misdescribes the test: the required dwell need not be served in one place, because POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed toward the 300 second minimum.

Accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) is available on this record because EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION: an LTA DataMall full-day bus lane on Orchard Road and Orchard Turn in force 17:00-20:00, with TrafficMarshals and enforcement cameras active, whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the whole 18:38-18:52 trip window. The limb's distance qualification is met too - the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 178.95 m, inside the 300 m leash. The trace's larger whole-run maximum of 1191.8 m is not a position inside either in-geofence hold (a hold is by definition within 120 m of the pin) but a start-of-trace approach figure, the trace opening at 18:39:05, five minutes before the 18:44:30 arrival.

The driver's own chat account of why he moved - that the marshal made him move because the bus lane runs until 8pm, and that he told the rider he was going one round and coming back to the same place - is corroborated by the LTA advisory for exactly that road and window, and the trace matches it fix for fix: he leaves the geofence at 18:47:35 and is back inside it at 18:49:35, a 120 second loop whose furthest point is 178.95 m from the pin, followed by a further 185 second hold. That is a driver complying with a no-stopping kerb, which is the very situation POL-NS-06(i) was drafted to cover, not a driver abandoning the pickup.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on the trip record's own fields: the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, five seconds after the last qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:52:40, and there is no boarding event anywhere in the record - started_at and ended_at are both null. RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes the limb recognises, and the recorded wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is consistent with the 18:44:30 arrival marker and the 18:52:45 cancellation.

The rider's own track places her device between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pickup pin across all 70 fixes in the waiting window, at zero speed throughout, and the qualifying rider fix count against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius is nil. She was not at the pickup and not approaching it at any moment before cancellation. That answers 'I was coming down for you' and removes limb (c) of POL-NS-04 from the case: the rider-exoneration route cannot be run on this trace.

Independently of presence, POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver answered inside the 120 second window: the rider's 'ok coming down now' was sent at 18:46:20 and the driver's reply - that the marshal had moved him and he was going one round and returning to the same place - was sent at 18:47:50, 90 seconds later. Limb (b) therefore fails, and any residual coordination question is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06 rather than by exonerating the rider.

POL-NS-03 has no purchase on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary for the required dwell outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's two stationary holds are inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius at a pickup with a single registered point (venue_id VEN-ION-ORCHARD, registered_pickup_points 1), so no wrong-entrance, wrong-block or pin-ambiguity case arises and no goodwill payment is in issue.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is compensated at 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, that is SGD 3.20, under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, below the threshold of 0.08. The clause requires both limbs and neither is met, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The SGD 4.00 actually charged reconciles under POL-NS-08(d): it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00, the two dimensions agreeing, so there is no fare defect and no basis for splitting the fee. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the correct disposition of the contested amount is that the present charge stands, with the SGD 3.20 driver payment recorded as an independent, platform-funded figure per POL-GEN-03 and never netted against the rider's fee.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged, so this case is decidable on the record and the fee should not be placed on hold. The two admissible traces agree rather than contradict (arrival 18:44:30, cancellation 18:52:45, 8.3 minutes); every one of the seven artifacts in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence; the parties share no other no-show dispute in the trailing 90 days, both disputes_with_counterparty_90d being 0; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3.

ruling.explanation:
Your $4.00 no-show cancellation fee stands and is not refunded, and the driver is paid $3.20 (80% of that $4.00 fee) by the platform.

Why the fee stands. The fee is chargeable only if the driver held position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous 300 seconds - the minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. You are right that the driver's own 10-second GPS trace (EV-GPS-00214) shows two separate holds - 170 seconds from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds from 18:49:35 - and neither alone reaches 300 seconds. But POL-NS-06(i) permits the two in-geofence intervals to be counted together where the driver circled a restricted kerb and never strayed more than 300 m from the pin. Both conditions are met on this record: the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00214-01 carries type KERB_RESTRICTION, covers the pickup road and is in force 17:00-20:00, over the whole 18:38-18:52 window; and the driver's furthest point between the two holds was 179.0 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. The larger 1,191.8 m figure in the trace is the driver's approach to Orchard before he reached the bay at all, not a position during the pickup attempt, so it does not break the leash. Added together the dwell is 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the required minimum, so POL-NS-06 yields no refund.

On the arrival marker: the driver tapped 'arrived' at 18:44:30, 15 seconds before the first in-geofence fix at 18:44:45. That is within one sampling interval, and it is not a false arrival - the driver was not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or more. Under POL-NS-05(iii) the waiting clock is recomputed to run from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45, and because the corrected dwell of 355 seconds still exceeds the 300 second minimum, the marker does not defeat the fee.

The other refund routes do not apply. POL-NS-04 fails: the driver replied to your 18:46:20 message at 18:47:50, 90 seconds later, inside the 120-second window, and in any event your device remained 691-717 m from the pin with no qualifying fix inside the 150 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-03 does not apply because ION Orchard has a single registered pickup point and the driver's holds were inside the 120 m arrival radius. Your assertion that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' misdescribes the test, which expressly permits the intervals to be summed.

Money and checks. The $4.00 charged reconciles: it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so there is no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d). Driver compensation is 80% of the $4.00 fee, i.e. $3.20 (POL-NS-07); the anti-farming check does not trip because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2 of 118 completed trips is 0.017 (below 0.08). No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger applies: the trip record and GPS trace agree on arrival and cancellation, every artifact in the bundle is complete at weight 1.0, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence, the two parties share no prior no-show dispute in the trailing 90 days, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1. The driver's $3.20 is platform-funded and never netted against your fee.

Between the holds he went no further than 179 m from the pin, inside the 300 m limit that guards the rule. Your point that he never stayed 5 minutes in one place is true of each hold taken separately, but the two are properly summed. Your reliance on the 1,191.8 m maximum on the trace applies the 300 m limit to the driver's whole drive to the pickup (the trace opens at 18:39:05, five minutes before his 18:44:30 arrival) instead of to his movement between the holds, and that reading would make the summing rule unusable in any real pickup. On timing: you are right that the 'arrived' tap at 18:44:30 is 15 seconds before the first in-geofence fix at 18:44:45, but that is within one and a half sampling intervals and far inside the 90-second tolerance POL-NS-08(a) sets for matching the marker to the trace; the marker is not FALSE under POL-NS-05 (the driver was not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or more), and POL-NS-01(c) measures the waiting clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the tap, so the 355-second dwell is unaffected. Your own device log shows your phone stationary about 690-717 m from the pickup across all 70 fixes, never inside the 150 m presence radius, which is consistent with the driver's account that you said you were coming down and never came. POL-NS-04 does not assist you (the driver replied within 90 seconds). Driver: your account is accepted in full. POL-NS-03, POL-NS-04 and POL-NS-05 do not apply. POL-NS-07 therefore pays you 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, with SGD 0.80 retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip - driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2/118 = 0.017 (below 0.08) - so compensation is paid rather than withheld. POL-NS-09 is not engaged: the traces agree, no artifact is impaired (all seven are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped below 1.0), the parties share no other no-show dispute in the trailing 90 days, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1. No clause produces a referral. Per POL-GEN-03, amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.20 figure because this is a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling; it is the driver's payment, not a refund to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your $4.00 no-show charge stands, and no part of it is refunded to you. To the driver: you are owed SGD 3.20. The reasoning follows.

MONEY. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00214) shows a cancellation fee of SGD 4.00, payment status CHARGED, refund issued 0.00. That figure reconciles under POL-NS-08(d): it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), the two dimensions agreeing, so there is no fare defect and no basis for splitting the fee.

WHY THE FEE IS CHARGEABLE. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on this record. (a) EV-TRIP-00214 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:44:30. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00214) places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius sold by POL-NS-02 — 40 qualifying in-radius fixes. The first in-radius fix is at 18:44:45, one 10-second sampling interval after the 18:44:30 marker. That sub-interval difference does not make the marker false: POL-NS-05, the clause that polices premature arrival taps, fires only where the driver is more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h or above at the marker, and neither holds (the driver's furthest point anywhere in the pickup is 178.95 m). Consistently with POL-NS-01(c), the waiting clock is run from GPS entry into the geofence at 18:44:45, not from the tap. (c) The trace records two in-geofence holds — 170 s (18:44:45 to 18:47:35) and 185 s (18:49:35 to 18:52:40) — 355 s accumulated against the 300 s LARGE_VENUE minimum, a surplus of 55 s (shortfall_sec -55). (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had accrued, with no boarding event (started_at and ended_at both null).

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' accounts and the platform telemetry line up on the material facts. The driver marked arrival at 18:44:30, held at the ION PHV bay for 170 seconds (18:44:45 to 18:47:35), was moved off the kerb by the marshal because the Orchard Road bus lane was in force until 20:00, drove a 120-second loop that took him no further than 178.95 m from the pin, re-entered the bay at 18:49:35 and held a further 185 seconds until 18:52:40, then cancelled at 18:52:45 recording RIDER_NO_SHOW. Nothing was boarded (started_at and ended_at are null).

To the rider: (1) You say he never stayed five minutes in one place. The 300-second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup need not be served continuously in one spot: POL-NS-06(i) lets separate in-geofence intervals be summed where an LTA advisory covers the pickup road and the driver never went more than 300 m from the pin. EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is a populated KERB_RESTRICTION (full-day bus lane, Orchard Road/Orchard Turn, 17:00 to 20:00, marshals and cameras active) covering the whole trip window, and the driver's furthest point between the two holds was 178.95 m, inside the 300 m leash. The summed dwell is 355 seconds, 55 seconds above the 300-second minimum, so POL-NS-06 produces no shortfall and no refund. (2) You point to the trace's 1,191.8 m maximum distance. That figure is from the driver's approach before he reached the bay (the trace opens at 18:39:05, roughly five minutes before arrival), not from the leaving-and-re-entering the leash governs; inside the pickup attempt the maximum is 178.95 m. (3) You note the first in-geofence fix (18:44:45) is 15 seconds after the 18:44:30 marker. POL-NS-02 makes limb (b) fail only where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation; there are 40 qualifying in-radius fixes here, so arrival is established, and any marker imprecision is handled by POL-NS-05(iii) - the clock runs from the first qualifying fix and the corrected dwell still exceeds the minimum. (4) The 8.3-minute wait_time_min is elapsed time from the marker to cancellation, not dwell; the dwell measured from the trace is 355 seconds. POL-NS-04 does not assist you either: the driver replied 90 seconds after your 18:46:20 message, inside the 120-second window, so that clause does not run.

To the driver: your arrival is established on the 40 qualifying in-radius fixes, the KERB_RESTRICTION advisory supports accumulating your two holds, and limb (d) is satisfied (you terminated the trip with RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event is recorded). The anti-farming check does not trip - no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2 divided by 118 completed trips is 0.017 (below 0.08) - so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The amount: the contested charge of SGD 4.00 stands. It reconciles with the greater of the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, so there is no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d). Under POL-NS-07 you are compensated at 80 per cent of that fee, SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00, funded by the platform and not netted against the rider's charge. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged (all seven artifacts are complete at weight 1.0, the traces agree, and neither party has another no-show dispute with the other in the trailing 90 days), so nothing is held and no referral is produced. The rider's claim is not supported on the evidence and the present charge stands.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and the driver must carry limb (c) on its own words: he must have 'held position inside that geofence for a continuous dwell of at least' the 300 seconds the fee schedule sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The driver's own 10-second telemetry records exactly two in-geofence holds, 170 seconds from 18:44:45 and 185 seconds from 18:49:35, each reported as a separate run. The longest continuous hold anywhere in this pickup is 185 seconds, 115 seconds short of the minimum, and the rider's description of a car that 'kept moving around' and never 'stayed 5 minutes in one place' is precisely what the trace records.

The only route by which the driver reaches 300 seconds is the summing of the two holds permitted by POL-NS-06(i), and that permission is conditional: the trace must show the driver leaving and re-entering the arrival radius 'without at any point travelling more than 300 m from the pin'. Over this pickup (18:39:05 to 18:52:40) the trace summary reports a maximum distance from the pin of 1,191.8 m - some four times the leash - and a total track of 3.0 km. The smaller 179.0 m figure reported for the inter-interval excursion is not the driver's maximum range on the trace. If the leash is applied to the trace as its words 'at any point' require, the condition for accumulation is not made out, the intervals cannot be summed, and the effective dwell remains the single 185-second hold.

Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the POL-NS-02 geofence at or before the timestamp of the arrival event. The event is logged at 18:44:30, while the earliest qualifying in-radius fix on the driver's own trace opens the first qualifying run at 18:44:45 - fifteen seconds later, and more than one 10-second sampling interval behind the marker. The record therefore carries no admissible in-radius fix at or before the marker to support the condition that marker certifies, and the waiting clock under POL-NS-01(c) runs from the first qualifying fix at 18:44:45, not from the marker.

trip_record.wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is not dwell: it is elapsed time from the 18:44:30 marker to the 18:52:45 cancellation, 495 seconds in all. Across that period the trace accounts for only 355 seconds inside the arrival radius; the balancing 140 seconds is time outside the geofence, including the 120-second loop between 18:47:35 and 18:49:35 during which the driver reached 179 m from the pin and speeds of up to 49.6 km/h. A 'wait' figure built on the marker cannot supply the continuous 300-second hold POL-NS-01(c) requires.

The rider does not press POL-NS-04, and says so plainly rather than stretching it: her 18:46:20 message was followed by the driver's 18:47:50 reply, ninety seconds later, so limb (b)'s 120-second-silence requirement is not met and the clause cannot run in her favour. This case is decided on the dwell arithmetic under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06, not on the contact clause.

The contested sum is the cancellation-fee line alone. fare_breakdown shows a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Where the effective dwell falls short of the POL-NS-01 minimum for the zone class, POL-NS-06 refunds that line to the rider in full and states that no driver compensation is payable. The rider seeks SGD 4.00 returned and no compensation paid out of it; the fee is the only amount the ledger moved.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-08-07T18:44:30, and the GPS trace then places the driver inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius of 120 m from 18:44:45, generating 40 qualifying in-radius fixes across two separate holds (18:44:45-18:47:35 and 18:49:35-18:52:40). That is far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires before arrival is deemed established, so POL-NS-01 limb (a) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are both satisfied on the trace's own numbers.

There is no false arrival marker to attack. Nothing in the record places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h or above at the 18:44:30 marker: the derived excursion block measures the driver's furthest point between the two holds at 178.95 m, and it records the POL-NS-06(i) limb as available rather than flagging any false-arrival condition. Even on the rider's best case that the marker preceded the first in-radius fix by a single 10 second sampling interval, POL-NS-05(iii) applies: the waiting clock is recomputed to the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:44:45, and because the corrected dwell still exceeds the 300 second minimum the false marker does not by itself defeat the fee.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 355 accumulated seconds - two holds of 170 s and 185 s - against the LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 s. The derived shortfall is minus 55 seconds, meaning there is no shortfall at all, so POL-NS-06 returns no refund. The rider's assertion that the driver 'never even stayed 5 minutes in one place' misdescribes the test: the required dwell need not be served in one place, because POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed toward the 300 second minimum.

Accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) is available on this record because EV-ADVIS-00214-01 is present and populated with type KERB_RESTRICTION: an LTA DataMall full-day bus lane on Orchard Road and Orchard Turn in force 17:00-20:00, with TrafficMarshals and enforcement cameras active, whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the whole 18:38-18:52 trip window. The limb's distance qualification is met too - the driver's furthest point between the intervals was 178.95 m, inside the 300 m leash. The trace's larger whole-run maximum of 1191.8 m is not a position inside either in-geofence hold (a hold is by definition within 120 m of the pin) but a start-of-trace approach figure, the trace opening at 18:39:05, five minutes before the 18:44:30 arrival.

The driver's own chat account of why he moved - that the marshal made him move because the bus lane runs until 8pm, and that he told the rider he was going one round and coming back to the same place - is corroborated by the LTA advisory for exactly that road and window, and the trace matches it fix for fix: he leaves the geofence at 18:47:35 and is back inside it at 18:49:35, a 120 second loop whose furthest point is 178.95 m from the pin, followed by a further 185 second hold. That is a driver complying with a no-stopping kerb, which is the very situation POL-NS-06(i) was drafted to cover, not a driver abandoning the pickup.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on the trip record's own fields: the trip was terminated by the driver at 18:52:45 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, five seconds after the last qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:52:40, and there is no boarding event anywhere in the record - started_at and ended_at are both null. RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes the limb recognises, and the recorded wait_time_min of 8.3 minutes is consistent with the 18:44:30 arrival marker and the 18:52:45 cancellation.

The rider's own track places her device between 690.7 m and 717.2 m from the pickup pin across all 70 fixes in the waiting window, at zero speed throughout, and the qualifying rider fix count against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius is nil. She was not at the pickup and not approaching it at any moment before cancellation. That answers 'I was coming down for you' and removes limb (c) of POL-NS-04 from the case: the rider-exoneration route cannot be run on this trace.

Independently of presence, POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver answered inside the 120 second window: the rider's 'ok coming down now' was sent at 18:46:20 and the driver's reply - that the marshal had moved him and he was going one round and returning to the same place - was sent at 18:47:50, 90 seconds later. Limb (b) therefore fails, and any residual coordination question is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06 rather than by exonerating the rider.

POL-NS-03 has no purchase on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary for the required dwell outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's two stationary holds are inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius at a pickup with a single registered point (venue_id VEN-ION-ORCHARD, registered_pickup_points 1), so no wrong-entrance, wrong-block or pin-ambiguity case arises and no goodwill payment is in issue.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is compensated at 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, that is SGD 3.20, under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 118 is 0.017, below the threshold of 0.08. The clause requires both limbs and neither is met, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

The SGD 4.00 actually charged reconciles under POL-NS-08(d): it is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00, the two dimensions agreeing, so there is no fare defect and no basis for splitting the fee. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute the correct disposition of the contested amount is that the present charge stands, with the SGD 3.20 driver payment recorded as an independent, platform-funded figure per POL-GEN-03 and never netted against the rider's fee.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged, so this case is decidable on the record and the fee should not be placed on hold. The two admissible traces agree rather than contradict (arrival 18:44:30, cancellation 18:52:45, 8.3 minutes); every one of the seven artifacts in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence; the parties share no other no-show dispute in the trailing 90 days, both disputes_with_counterparty_90d being 0; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3.
